title: HF5006 (2025-2026 Regular): Peace officer required to conduct testing of a person suspected of carrying a firearm while under the influence, penalty for carrying a firearm with an elevated blood alcohol concentration increased, and length of time a person is prohibited from carrying a firearm after conviction increased.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2026-04-16; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/94/2026/0/HF/5006/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version, 2026-04-16. No votes recorded. The bill strikes the 'may' (officer discretion), the 'second or subsequent violation' wording, and the 180-day suspension, and renumbers clauses; paragraph (c) and the rest of (d) are not quoted.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7142, subd. 3): When an officer authorized under subdivision 2 to make arrests has reason to believe that the person may be violating or has violated subdivision 1, the officer must require the person to provide a breath sample for a preliminary screening test using a device approved by the commissioner for this purpose.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7142, subd. 3): If the results of the preliminary screening test indicate that the person is violating subdivision 1, the officer must require the chemical tests authorized in section 624.7143.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7142, subd. 6): (b) A person who violates subdivision 1, clause (5), is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. If the person was previously convicted of violating this section, the person is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7142, subd. 6): (d) In addition to the penalty imposed under paragraph (b), if a person violates subdivision 1, clause (5), the person's authority to carry a pistol in a public place on or about the person's clothes or person under the provisions of a permit or otherwise is revoked and the person may not reapply for a period of five years from the date of conviction.
